questions.text:
Consider the following two statements about database transaction schedules:

I. Strict two-phase locking protocol generates conflict serializable schedules that are also recoverable.
II. Timestamp-ordering concurrency control protocol with Thomas' Write Rule can generate view serializable schedules that are not conflict serializable.

Which of the above statements is/are TRUE?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Strict 2PL holds all exclusive locks until commit, so schedules are conflict serializable and no transaction reads uncommitted data [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] recoverable [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- Thomas' write rule ignores obsolete writes, which allows some view serializable schedules that are not conflict serializable (blind writes) [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.

Answer: Both I and II

questions.text: Let G be an undirected complete graph on n vertices, where n[latex]\gt[/latex]2. Then, the number of different Hamiltonian cycles in G is equal to
questions.solution:
Fix one vertex as the start. The remaining n [latex]-[/latex] 1 vertices can be arranged in (n [latex]-[/latex] 1)! orders, and each cycle is counted twice (two directions).

Number of Hamiltonian cycles [latex]=\frac{(n-1)!}{2}[/latex]

Answer: [latex]\frac{(n-1)!}{2}[/latex]

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

Factor both and cancel (x [latex]-[/latex] 3):
[latex]\frac{(x-3)(x+3)(x^2+9)}{(x-3)(2x+1)}=\frac{(x+3)(x^2+9)}{2x+1}[/latex]

At x = 3: [latex]\frac{6\times18}{7}=\frac{108}{7}[/latex]

Answer: 108/7

questions.text: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct about the [latex]B^+[/latex] tree data structure used for creating an index of a relational database table?
questions.solution:
In a [latex]B^+[/latex] tree only the leaf nodes hold pointers to data records. Non-leaf nodes contain only keys and pointers to child nodes.

The other statements are true (height balanced, sorted keys, leaves linked).

Answer: Non-leaf nodes have pointers to data records

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: Non-leaf nodes have pointers to data records
Key values in each node are kept in sorted order
Each leaf node has a pointer to the next leaf node

questions.text:
For [latex]\Sigma =\{a,b\}[/latex], let us consider the regular language
[latex]L=\{x|x=a^{2+3k} \; or \; x=b^{10+12k}, k\geq 0\}[/latex].
Which one of the following can be a pumping length (the constant guaranteed by the pumping lemma) for L?
questions.solution:
p must be larger than any string that cannot be pumped.
- [latex]b^{10}[/latex] cannot be pumped: removing any part gives fewer than 10 b's, which is not in L. So p must be at least 11 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 3, 5, 9 fail.
- With p = 24: every b-string of length [latex]\ge24[/latex] (34, 46, [latex]\ldots[/latex]) can pump [latex]y=b^{12}[/latex] inside the first 24 symbols, and every a-string can pump [latex]y=aaa[/latex].

Answer: 24
